question.problem:
Given that 
$B=[\begin{aligned}3 & 9 \\ 7 & 20\end{aligned}]$ 
has the LU decomposition $B=LU$, then ${l}_{21}\cdot {u}_{12}=$
question.worked_solution:
To find the matrices $L$ and $U,$ we reduce the matrix $B$ to row echelon form. Whilst doing this, we simultaneously write down the row operations applied to $B$ in terms of matrix multiplication using elementary matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}B & =[\begin{aligned}3 & 9 \\ 7 & 20\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+(-\frac{7}{3}){R}_{1}\,⟺\,\overset{{E}_{1}}{\overset{⏞}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -\frac{7}{3} & 1\end{aligned}]}}\cdot B \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 9 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =U\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix is upper triangular, so it is our matrix $U.$ Now, since ${E}_{1}B=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{1}B & =U \\ B & ={E}_{1}^{-1}U \\ B & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -\frac{7}{3} & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ B & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ \frac{7}{3} & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}{{[\begin{aligned}3 & 9 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{U}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${l}_{21}=\frac{7}{3},{u}_{12}=9,$ and ${l}_{21}\cdot {u}_{12}=21.$
